`person:group-kk-birla-mp-birla` · flag: **mixed (MP Birla); mostly-clean (Chambal/Avadh)** · confidence: single-source · tickers: CHAMBLFERT, AVADHSUGAR, MAGADSUGAR, HTMEDIA, BIRLACORPN, UNIVCABLES, VINDHYATEL, ZUARI

Flag: MIXED (MP Birla, litigation overhang) / MOSTLY-CLEAN (KK Birla companies). KK Birla group (after K.K. Birla d. 2008, split among daughters): Chambal Fertilisers (Saroj Poddar side; also Zuari Agro via Adventz), Avadh Sugar & Energy and Magadh Sugar (Nandini Nopany side; Upper Ganges/Oudh demerged 2015), HT Media (Shobhana Bhartia). Chambal is a cash-generative, dividend-paying fertiliser company; its 2025 buyback is a positive (unverified detail). HT Media has had persistent losses and complex RPTs with promoter-linked digital/radio entities -- minority value has eroded (unverified specifics). MP Birla group: Priyamvada Birla (d. Jul-2004) willed her estate, which controls Birla Corp, Universal Cables, Vindhya Telelinks, Birla Cable, to her CA R.S. Lodha; the Birla family (KK, BK, GP, SK, KM, Yashovardhan Birla) challenged the will. 20+ years of litigation: court-appointed administrators pendente lite (2012); a Calcutta HC division bench (Dec-2023) held that the estate is limited to shares she held, not controlling interests in companies -- appeal to the Supreme Court expected. Harsh Lodha has continued to run the companies. Lesson: a contested will over control can freeze strategic decisions and invite boardroom litigation for decades. Confidence: single-source for most KK Birla details.

- **red flags:** two-decade will dispute; HT Media losses/RPTs (unverified)

Sources:

body: Cummins India Ltd (CIL) designs, makes, sells and services diesel/gas engines (and some gensets) from 16 hp to 4,500 hp. The parent, **Cummins Inc. (CMI), holds 51.00%** and has done so since at least 2017 `[SCR]`. CIL does **not** make most gensets itself. It sells engines to **three Genset OEMs (GOEMs, e.g. Sudhir Power and Jakson)**, which add an alternator, enclosure and controls. It also sells to industrial OEMs (excavators, compressors, rail, mining, marine, defence) and through **21 dealers with 120+ branches** `[WEB: cummins.com India page]`. "480 customer touchpoints" `[PR-Q2]`. A large part of what it sells is *bought from sister companies*: Tata Cummins (a 50:50 JV of CMI and Tata Motors) and Cummins Technologies India (CTIPL, a CMI subsidiary).

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Power Gen domestic | 4,758 (+24%) | 1,340 | 1,424 | **1,308** | −2% |
| Distribution (aftermarket, parts, service) | 3,278 (+22%) | 796 | 886 | **900** | +13% |
| Industrial domestic | 1,650 (−1%) | n/a | 458 | **406** | +5% |
| HHP exports | 984 (+20%) | 279 | ~298 [EST: 268/0.9] | **268** | −4% |
| LHP exports | ~1,005 [EST: 1,989 total exports − 984] | n/a | ~181 [EST] | **226** | +3% |
| Total sales (ex other op. revenue) | 11,950 | 3,122 | 3,375 | 3,247 | +4% |

- **Inside Power Gen, Q2 FY27** `[CC-Q2FY27]`: LHP ₹98 cr, mid-range ₹236 cr, heavy duty ₹142 cr, and the remaining **~₹832 cr (64%) is HHP + DC**.
- **DC share of power gen over time:** ~10% (Q1 FY25 `[CC-Q1FY25]`) → 23% (Q1 FY26) → ~25% (Q3 FY26) → 30–35% for FY26, ~35% in Q4 → **40% (Q1 FY27)** → "30–40%" (Q2 FY27). So **DC ≈ ₹1,430–1,670 cr in FY26** [EST: 30–35% × 4,758] and **≈ ₹390–520 cr in Q2 FY27**.
- **Ex-DC power gen is ambiguous by design.** A Macquarie analyst pointed out that at 30% DC share, ex-DC growth was mid-teens, and at 40% it was negative `[CC-Q2FY27]`. Management gave a range, not a number. **Definition audit (technique #10): "30–40%" is a 10-point band on a ₹1,308 cr line, so ±₹130 cr. That is wide enough to hide a non-DC slowdown.**
- **Industrial, Q2 FY27:** construction 131, rail 117, compressor 54, mining 49, marine 27, rest defence/O&G/parts `[CC-Q2FY27]`.
- **Exports by region, Q2 FY27:** Europe 29%, LatAm 28%, APAC 22%, Middle East 15% `[CC-Q2FY27]`.
